title: Holes and Drops: A Lidar Tipped Down Sees the Ground at a Known Range, So Ground That Is Not There Is a Hole, and How Fast It Can Be Driven at Depends on How Far Away the Ground Is Seen

artifact.note: the range at which a lidar tipped down by an angle at a height sees flat ground in each direction, the classification of a beam against it (ground, a hole or a drop where it is longer or absent, raised where it is shorter), the distance to the nearest hole, the widest hole that can fall between two scans of a moving vehicle, and the fastest speed from which the vehicle can stop before a hole that is seen only at that distance
